D006-D010_h001.question:
"It's been a rough ten months, doctor. I've found myself getting so easily agitated, snapping at colleagues over the smallest things at work. I'm an IT auditor, and usually, I’m meticulous, but lately, I’ve been starting countless projects, jumping from one spreadsheet to another, convinced I’m on the verge of some major breakthrough, but never quite finishing anything. My boss has noticed the drop in my productivity, and honestly, it’s impacting my job.

And then there are these… sensations. For about eight months now, I keep feeling like something is crawling on my skin, or that someone is lightly touching me, especially when I'm in the middle of these high-energy phases. I try to brush it off, but it’s unsettling.

I've also started hearing new words in my head, 'flexadigm' and 'quantivance,' that seem to hold deep meaning, but I can’t explain them to anyone. And I’m constantly looking over my shoulder, certain that my former employer is out to get me, monitoring my every move. These strange feelings and beliefs, the skin sensations and the feeling of being watched, they only ever pop up when I'm feeling this wired and irritable.

Before all this, around three months ago, I went through a really dark period. I just wanted to be left alone, stopped calling friends, and felt like it would be easier if I just didn't wake up some mornings. My social life completely ground to a halt then."

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder

D006-D010_h002.question:
"It's been... well, it's hard to keep track, but I'd say for about ten months now, things have been really strange. There are times I feel incredibly alive, euphoric almost, like I'm bursting with energy. I can't sit still; I just want to keep going and going. My mind races, jumping from one thought to the next, and if a book drops in the next room, or someone coughs, my attention just zips right over there, completely pulled away from whatever I was doing. It's like my brain is too wide open to everything around me.

But then, during those high periods, that's when things get really weird, you know? For the last eight months, when I'm feeling that intense energy, I start seeing things—people who aren't there, objects moving in the corners of my vision. And I get this overwhelming feeling that I'm being watched, that someone is always trying to get into my research or follow me home. It makes it almost impossible to concentrate at the archives; my thoughts get so jumbled, sometimes my sentences don't even make sense.

Then, there are other times, maybe three months ago, when all that fades, and I just sink into this deep, uninterested state. Nothing brings me joy, nothing at all. I tried to... well, I tried to end things, because it felt like there was no other way out. It’s important to understand that those really bizarre perceptions, the ones that make my thoughts so wild, they only happen when my mood is soaring like that. They’re like companions to that manic energy, they don’t just hang around on their own."
D006-D010_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder
D006-D010_h002.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

My wife says I'm insufferable, snapping at everyone, even the kids, for the smallest things. There are times I just feel so restless.

But the weirder stuff... for the past nine months, I've been seeing things, little shadowy figures moving in my peripheral vision, and my stomach... I just know there's something seriously wrong inside, something decaying away, even though the doctors say I'm fine. I've also been making some impulsive decisions, like getting into situations that are really out of character for a married man my age. But it didn't use to be like this. Before this frantic energy kicked in, for about six months, I was just... flat. Everything felt gray. I gained almost twenty pounds because all I wanted to do was sleep, sometimes twelve hours a night. Talking felt like wading through mud, and my sentences would just trail off. Now, it's like I swing between those two extremes. The hallucinations and those strange thoughts about my body only ever happen when I’m in one of these super-charged, irritable moods."

D006-D010_h022.question:
Lately, everything just feels… off. I’ve been feeling really down for about six months now, just a constant gloom that I can't shake. I’m always tired, even though I'm waking up hours before my alarm, staring at the ceiling. When people ask me how I'm doing, it’s like my brain just can’t form the words quickly enough. I’ve also put on a good bit of weight, which doesn’t help my mood.

Before this, though, things were different. For about a year, I was flying high. I felt amazing, like I could conquer anything. I was juggling so many clients, taking on new projects that my colleagues thought were impossible. I barely needed any sleep, just a few hours, and I'd wake up feeling completely refreshed, ready to tackle the day. That’s when the ideas started really flowing, but my speech sometimes got a bit wild. I’d be talking to clients, and the words would just connect based on their sound, like "client, reliant, defiant," rather than what I meant to say. I know I also spent way too much money during that time, just buying things impulsively without thinking about my already strained finances. It was hard to keep up with work sometimes because I felt so detached from others; I just wasn’t interested in socializing at all.

This past year, for about nine months of it, things got really strange during that high period. I started seeing figures lurking in the corners of my vision and became convinced that the world was going to end, and that a grand catastrophe was coming. It was all so vivid and real to me at the time, but the sightings and those chilling thoughts, they only really happened when I was feeling that intense energy, that elevated mood. They never popped up when I was feeling alright or even during this current low period. It's like they were part of the whole manic rush, if that makes sense.
D006-D010_h022.options:
A. Binge-Eating Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D006-D010_h023.question: It's been a rough year, doc. About a year ago, I started feeling… wired. My boss at the factory line said I was moving too fast, making mistakes, but I felt great, like I could finally keep up with all the quotas on the night shift. I'd come home at 6 AM, sleep maybe two hours, and I’d be up cleaning the whole apartment, scrubbing floors, pacing back and forth, my mind racing. I completely emptied my savings, buying all sorts of junk online that I definitely didn't need – just felt right at the time, you know? But then, maybe nine months ago, things got really strange. I started hearing these whispers, usually when I was alone, sometimes telling me the machines at work were going to explode, or that the world was about to be swallowed whole. It was like my mind was linking words just by how they sounded, not what they meant – like "stack and track and smack and crack." All this only happened when I was feeling that intense energy, that "wired" feeling. After about a year of that, things shifted again. For the last six months, it’s been the complete opposite. I can barely get myself out of bed for work; everything feels like wading through mud. My speech has slowed down, and sometimes it takes me ages to answer a simple question. I just feel like crying all the time, for no reason. My night terrors are back, waking me up in a cold sweat, and I’ve lost a lot of weight because I just don’t have an appetite anymore. It’s hard to show how I feel; my face just doesn't seem to move much anymore, even when I'm heartbroken. It's really affecting my ability to do my job, no matter what phase I’m in.

D006-D010_h024.question:
"Lately, it feels like my mind is playing tricks on me. For about a year now, I've had these surges of energy where I barely sleep – maybe an hour or two a night – but I never feel tired. I get this buzzing sensation, always needing to be doing something, always on the go. Even at work, in the data center, I'm constantly pacing, fiddling with equipment. Socially, I've been a whirlwind, emailing and calling everyone I know, even people I haven’t spoken to in years. It’s like I can’t stop myself from being the life of the party, even if it sometimes turns into snapping at people over minor things. I've also been doing some really reckless stuff, like taking my motorcycle out for joyrides at 3 AM, hitting ridiculous speeds.

The really disturbing part, though, has been these last nine months, *strictly during these high-energy periods*. I’ve started seeing things, like shadowy figures darting in my peripheral vision in the server aisles. And my girlfriend… I just know she’s seeing someone else. I look for clues everywhere, in her texts, her schedule, even little gestures. There's no solid proof, but my gut tells me. When I try to explain this, sometimes my words just get jumbled, and I can’t make sense.

Then, there are the crashes. For about six months, I’ll be in a deep funk, everything feels gray. Nothing brings me joy anymore. The music I used to love, video games, nothing. My movements slow down, even walking feels like a chore. I’ve put on a good amount of weight, and I wake up hours before my alarm, just staring at the ceiling, unable to go back to sleep. But it's only when I'm in one of those manic phases that the other odd things, the seeing and the suspicions, come out."

    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D006-D010_h024.answer: B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006-D010_h025.question:
It’s been a crazy year, doctor. For the past twelve months, I’ve been on top of the world, just bubbling with energy. I barely sleep – maybe an hour or two a night, and I wake up feeling completely refreshed, ready to hit the ground running. I’ve never been this productive, selling more houses than ever, calling everyone in my contact list, feeling truly alive. Even my husband comments on how much I’m out there, always going, going, going. It feels amazing, like I can do anything! Sometimes I take on a little too much though, like that time I decided to invest in all those penny stocks without really looking into them. But what's life without a little risk, right?

But then there are these other things that have been happening, for about nine months now, only when I’m feeling this high. It's like my body isn't my own sometimes. I get this creeping, crawly feeling under my skin, like tiny insects moving around, even when there's nothing there. And I know it sounds strange, but I’ve been convinced there's something seriously wrong with my liver, like it's rotting from the inside, even though every test comes back normal. I try to explain it but the words get all jumbled, sometimes I just speak in rhymes, like "It's the liver, it shivers, delivers, but it withers." It’s hard to want to be around people when I’m feeling like this.

Before this energetic stretch, about six months ago, I was in a completely different place. I could barely get out of bed, felt like I was moving through molasses. My movements slowed down so much that even simple tasks became Monumental. I cried a lot, sometimes for no reason at all, and food just didn't appeal to me anymore. I'd just lie awake for hours, waiting for sleep to finally come.
D006-D010_h025.options:
A. Binge-Eating Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D006-D010_h025.answer: B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
